items.title: Separating the closure of the image of a closed set by an element congruent to one
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma produces an element which is congruent to one modulo an ideal of the source and whose image lies in a prescribed ideal of the target, under the hypothesis that the closure of the image of the closed set defined by that ideal is disjoint from the closed set defined by the source ideal. The proof names the ideal defining the closure of the image, uses disjointness of the two closed sets to see that the two ideals generate the unit ideal, writes the resulting decomposition of one, and then uses that the image of the first summand vanishes nowhere on the closed set defined by the target ideal, so that a power of that image lies in the target ideal; replacing the element by that power gives both required properties.
